newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse October turnover sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse October turnover sharply down.

text.p: Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) October turnover fell 23.7 percent to 122.53 million dinars ($24.54 million), the bourse said on Friday.
October activity raised the ten-month total turnover on the BSE to 1.9 billion dinars ($380 million).
The number of October deals inched down to 741 from 750 worth 160.597 million dinars a month ago, the bourse reported.

Traders blamed a decline on reduced market liquidity, dating from mid-September when the central bank launched a 10 percent reserve requirement. The measure drained between 250 and 300 million dinars from the banking system in September.
Traders were even more worried by recent central bank signals that the current reserve requirement might go up.
An increase (in the reserve requirement) would be another blow to the already illiquid market, traders said.
"This is a low volume market and key players (the banks) have insignificant mobile funds to play with," an analyst said.
Subdued market activity partly resulted from fears that the dinar may be devalued some time after the November 3 elections.
It was the first time ever the nascent financial market voiced sensitivity to developments other than liquidity.
In turn, the NBY unpopular measure drew minimal investor interest into its short-term bonds. Those accounted for only 9 percent of the monthly total turnover on the BSE.
NBY auctioned a new 50 million dinars tranche of its 30-day bonds on November 7. Until the end of October it sold bonds worth only 11.25 million.

Central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic told the daily Nasa Borba in an interview that the NBY did not worry about the low buying interest for its short-term bonds and said it meant investors had decided to devote funds to production instead.
Companies whose deposits help create bank liquidity are currently withdrawing funds to buy raw materials.
Banovic acknowledged that this drained liquidity from the banking system but said it signalled that investors were turning to real production.
The commercial paper segment was the leader of the month accounting for 69 percent of the monthly total turnover. There were 621 deals worth 84.87 million dinars.
Treasury bills followed, generating 12 percent of the monthly total in 78 transactions worth 14.35 million dinars.
Wheat selling forward contracts gained an 8 percent share in October. Ten deals fetched 9.76 million dinars.

Goran Altaras of the Belgrade bourse said investors finally began to wake up and expected buying activity to pick up towards December 3 -- the final deadline for the sale of 150 million dinars worth of contracts.
Certificates of deposits were traded 14 times for a volume of 2.29 million dinars. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
